title: Wrap — God knows all that can be known
source_text: XXX. Igitur conclusum esto, Deum perfecte & distincte novisse omnia, quae quomodocunque sciri & intelligi possunt, singularia & universalia, maxima & minima, patentia & latentia, bona & mala, praeterita, praesentia & futura, denique possibilia & impossibilia: quorum omnium quum aliquid mens humana percipiat, eorum nihil menti divinae atque infinitae potest non esse penitus cognitum & perceptum.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore let it be concluded that God has known perfectly and distinctly all things which in any way can be known and understood — singulars and universals, greatest and least, open and hidden, good and evil, past, present, and future, finally possibles and impossibles: of all which, when the human mind perceives something, nothing of them can fail to be thoroughly known and perceived by the divine and infinite mind.
pass_b_english: Close: perfect distinct knowledge of every knowable.
Past/present/future; possible/impossible — if humans glimpse any, God holds all.

lemmas.gloss: to have known all things perfectly and distinctly

choices.term: eorum nihil menti divinae atque infinitae potest non esse penitus cognitum & perceptum
choices.english: nothing of them can fail to be thoroughly known and perceived by the divine and infinite mind
choices.why: Honest object-slice close; next De Causa Praedestinationis.
rejected: some knowables escape the infinite mind
